title: Vendor capability spike: streaming, usage, resume, allowlists, rate-limit signals for claude, codex, grok
lead:
Measure what the claude, codex and grok CLIs actually do when run headless,
so the engine design rests on observed behavior. Every cell of the
capability table in docs/design.md is marked *unverified* today.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any Go code, the vendor adapters (S06), and forcing a real rate limit.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork launches every role headlessly on all three vendors with automatic
fallback (`scope.vendors`, `vendor.fallback`). That rests on five
behaviors nobody has measured: streamed events for the output tail, usage
and cost in the result, resume by session id, a per-tool allowlist, and a
rate-limit signal. If a vendor lacks one, v1 narrows for that vendor
instead of the whole build waiting (PROJECT.md, Risks).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `spike/` (new): throwaway zsh scripts, one per vendor. No Go, no go.mod.
- `testdata/vendors/<vendor>/` (new): redacted stdout, stderr, exit code
  and JSON for each probe.
- `docs/design.md`: the capability table and Vendors section.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
None: this slice writes no code. Each table cell must cite a fixture file
or say *unverified* with the reason.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- [HUMAN CHECK] Before any vendor call, the owner approves the call budget:
  about 6 calls per vendor, trivial prompts, cheapest model, run in a
  throwaway git repo under the scratch directory.
- Start from the invocations in `agents/setup/lib/workflow-vendor.sh:22-41`
  (`claude -p --output-format json`, `codex exec --json`,
  `grok --output-format json -p`, and the read-only flags).
- Per vendor, probe: a plain success; streamed output; a resume of that
  session by id; a run with a tool allowlist that denies a write; a
  read-only run asked to edit a file; and a forced failure (bad model
  name). Record exit code, stderr and the JSON fields for tokens and cost.
- Rate limits cannot be forced cheaply. Record the documented signal from
  each CLI's own help or docs, cite it, and mark the cell unverified.
- Redact key-like strings from every saved output (docs/state.md, Rules).
- Fill in the table. If a vendor lacks a needed capability, file an adj
  question on narrowing v1 for it; do not decide.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Every table cell cites a fixture under `testdata/vendors/` or is marked
  *unverified* with a reason.
- `rg -i 'sk-|api[_-]?key|token"\s*:\s*"[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}' testdata/` finds
  nothing.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit on the slice branch: "S01: vendor spike, capability table and
fixtures".
